channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: “The moment you take investor money, you lose control,” Jason Njoku tells African founders
item.description: Venture capital has become one of the loudest signals of startup success across Africa. Big rounds. Big valuations. Big headlines.

item.title: List of the most difficult African countries to collect debt
item.description: Debt recovery remains a challenge in several African countries, placing these countries on the global list of the 52 most difficult regions in which to reclaim outstanding debt.

item.title: South Africa’s largest paper manufacturer is shutting down amid rising import pressure
item.description: A leading South African paper and plastics manufacturer, MPact, has confirmed it will move ahead with retrenchments as it considers shutting down its paper mill in Springs, east of Johannesburg, highlighting the mounting pressures on the country’s manufacturing sector.

item.title: US moves to re-engage Sahel juntas as Russia tightens grip on Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso
item.description: The United States is recalibrating its approach to the Sahel as it seeks to reassert influence in Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, three military-led states that have increasingly aligned themselves with Russia following a wave of coups and diplomatic rifts with Western partners.

item.title: South Africa’s expulsion of Israeli diplomat sparks fresh US criticism
item.description: The United States on Tuesday criticised South Africa’s decision to expel Israel’s top diplomat last week, with a State Department spokesperson saying the move reflected a focus on what Washington called “grievance politics.”

item.title: Nigeria turns to China to help fix its broken refineries
item.description: Nigeria's state-owned oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC), recently revealed its plans to partner with a Chinese company to rehabilitate its dilapidated oil refineries.

item.title: African credit ratings climb to highest level since 2020 as growth improves
item.description: Economic reforms and stronger growth have lifted African sovereign credit ratings to their highest level in more than five years.

item.title: Afreximbank's newest member, South Africa, secures $8 billion lifeline for mining, auto and industrial growth
item.description: Africa’s largest trade finance institution, Afreximbank, has announced an initial $8 billion financing package for its newest member, South Africa, supporting projects across mining, automotive manufacturing, and industrial development.

item.title: Congo to export copper to Saudi Arabia, UAE with US support
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will export copper to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates through a U.S.-backed partnership with Mercuria Energy Group Ltd., as Washington seeks to challenge China’s dominance in critical metals.

item.title: Africa’s top 10 most import-dependent economies
item.description: Several African economies remain heavily dependent on imports, according to World Bank data, highlighting structural weaknesses that continue to leave the continent vulnerable to currency shocks, supply-chain disruptions, and global price volatility.
